page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is an Intel-based, memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv5 server family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 105 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration. A key hardware characteristic is its massive memory capacity of 672.0 GB, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 28.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on external Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong memory subsystem capabilities, with a PassMark memory score and large-block write memory bandwidth of 106.74 GB/sec both ranking in the top 25%. CPU-bound benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core performance, fall within the average range. The server demonstrates solid capabilities in low-parameter language model execution, achieving a strong text generation speed of 263.29 tokens/sec with a small 135M model, though performance scales down to an average 15.29 tokens/sec for medium 7B models.

The primary tradeoff of the E96-24s_v5 is its constrained CPU allocation relative to its memory footprint, which is designed to optimize software licensing costs for memory-intensive applications that do not scale linearly with core count. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency compared to local NVMe alternatives. This profile is highly suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-heavy data processing pipelines.
